cards.title: The crash is fixed

steps.text: the code took the first source line of a property with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. A type from another library has none, so it crashed.
it asks a new helper, `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation(item)`, instead.
a second place now uses `FirstOrDefault()` so it gets nothing instead of crashing.
when there is no source line, the helper gives back nothing (`FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax()`).
two new tests check that the code is still produced (`Assert.Contains(expectedResolverHintName, hintNames)`).

cards.verdict: The crash from the issue is fixed, and tests prove it.

cards.title: Some warnings are now silenced

steps.text: every warning went straight to `reportAnalyzerDiagnostic`.
every warning passes through `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` first.
the warning points at code in this project (`IsInSource` and `ContainsSyntaxTree`),

steps.text: the README says these warnings are `reported by the assembly that defines it`.
the warning page says the same: they are `reported by the project that defines that type`.
the code just drops them (`report(diagnostic)` runs only for this project's code).

cards.verdict: The notes describe the hidden warnings as fine, so they wait on the owner's choice about the filter.

rows: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.
